evidence: The noon word is analysed as two + watch/time-period, matching Platts do-pahar noon (dvi-prahara). Turner documents regional do/du/be two and pahar/pɔr/par watch, supporting the western bapor and eastern diphur contractions as qualified comparative members. Both components are represented; Turner’s suggestion that prahara may Sanskritize Persian pahra is retained as uncertainty about its deeper origin, not asserted as an established Sanskrit inheritance.

The complete compound is evening + time. Turner saṃdhyā explicitly gives eastern sā̃jh/sañjha, while velā gives Oriya beḷa daytime and eastern ber time (discussing l/r variation). Both ordered components are included; Pothwari sanyavɛlɛ is a qualified northwestern counterpart rather than the unrelated evening-star compound *saṃdhāvelaka.
The full expression is evening + watch/time period, saṃdhyā through sā̃j and prahara through pahar. Both lexical constituents are represented; prahara’s deeper history remains uncertain in Turner.

Turner *jhāla burning/pungent explicitly gives Assamese zāl and Bengali jhāl hot/pungent. These Hajong/Bengali forms match that eastern family; aspiration and the final vowel are preserved. Bishnupriya forms with an additional copula or other ending are not silently shortened.

Qualified members of the regional velā time/daylight family: Turner gives Assamese beli time, Oriya beḷa daytime and eastern ber/beri forms, while noting a probable Dravidian background with sun/daytime meanings. The surveys themselves attest the sun sense. This is a comparative family assignment with a daylight-to-sun semantic extension; regional contact and the exact transmission path remain open, especially in Hajong/Bishnupriya. Retroflex beṛ/beḍ forms are excluded because Turner also separates a *veḍā branch.
